title: The Spillover Effect of Social Capital Along the Supply Chain: Evidence from the Cost of Debt
authors: Yuyan Guan; Xing Li; Gerald J. Lobo; Haibin Wu
near_miss_reason: The only DiD in the paper (Table 4) is a stacked DiD around county sex-scandal shocks to major customers (Hilary and Huang 2023; event dates vary across the 163 stacks, loan years 1998-2005): reghdfe logspread inter treat post, absorb(sup_cust_id year bank_id loantype loanpurpose stack) cluster(sup_gvkey). Stacked designs are not admitted (PROTOCOL 5b: a paper reporting only stacked DiD is a near-miss); the column also includes an additive `post` main effect and additional additive FE (lead bank, loan type, loan purpose). Column 2 adds time-varying supplier/customer/loan controls; columns 3-4 use event-time bins (pre2 pre1 pst1 pst2 pst3) with post-bin main effects. The main analysis (Tables 1-3, 5-11) regresses loan spreads on a continuous customer social-capital index.
eligible_reason: No reported column is an unstacked TWFE/event study with only unit and calendar-time FE: the only DiD is stacked with a post main effect and extra additive FE; everything else uses a continuous regressor (wacust_lagsc) or IV.
design_notes: Loan-facility level data (DealScan) assigned to supplier-customer pairs (sup_cust_id). Table 4 (Code.do lines 264-287): did.dta with 1,657 facilities, 163 stacks, treat x post window gap in {-3..2} years around the scandal report date; globals at lines 107-114: indep1 = inter treat post; indep2 = inter_pre2 inter_pre1 inter_pst1 inter_pst2 inter_pst3 treat pre2 pre1 pst1 pst2 pst3; absob = sup_cust_id year bank_id loantype loanpurpose stack; clust = sup_gvkey. Baseline (Table 2): reghdfe logspread wacust_lagsc + controls, absorb(sup_indy_id bank_id loantype loanpurpose). Table 3: ivreghdfe with distance-to-border and ethnic-homogeneity instruments. Tables 5-11: cross-sectional splits, channel regressions (ppmlhdfe for patents), robustness.
estimators_reported: stacked_did (Table 4 cols 1-2) and stacked event-time bins (Table 4 cols 3-4)
n_adoption_cohorts_note: 163 stacks (treated supplier-customer pairs with their own scandal report dates; loan years 1998-2005). Exact number of distinct event dates not recoverable from did.dta (datereport dropped).
never_treated_note: Within each stack, control pairs (treat==0) are never treated.

specs.exclusion_reason: stacked DiD (stack FE); additive post main effect; additional additive FE (bank_id, loantype, loanpurpose); loan-level repeated cross-section
specs.treatment_var: inter = treat x post (with treat and post main effects)
specs.treatment_definition: treat = supplier whose major customer's county experienced a publicly reported sex scandal (Hilary-Huang 2023); post = loan facility starts on/after the report date (gap >= 0); window gap -3..2 years
specs.unit_var: sup_cust_id (supplier-customer pair); loans are the observations
specs.fe: sup_cust_id + year + bank_id + loantype + loanpurpose + stack
specs.controls: none in col 1 (post, treat main effects); col 2 adds $cotrl1 $cotrl2 $cotrl3 (time-varying supplier, customer, loan characteristics)
specs.sample_condition: did.dta: 1,657 facilities, 163 stacks, excluding financial/utility suppliers
specs.notes: Columns 3-4 (line 283-286): inter_pre2 inter_pre1 inter_pst1 inter_pst2 inter_pst3 with pre/post bin main effects.

data_files_note: Final analysis datasets (from licensed DealScan/Compustat/WRDS) are shipped as real data per README; intermediate 'Project Data' files referenced in Code.do are not included.
priority_note: Near-miss: stacked DiD only, with post main effect and extra FE; main design is not a DiD.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). Table 4 is a robustness/identification exercise; the stacked sample is small (261 treated loan-years). did.dta inspected with pandas: stack sizes 2-25 loans, year 1998-2005, gap -3..2.
